short: Self-educated clockmaker who solved the problem of calculating longitude at sea.
full:
John Harrison was a Yorkshire carpenter and clockmaker who dedicated his life to solving the "longitude problem" — the inability of sailors to determine their east-west position, which had caused numerous maritime disasters. The British government offered a massive £20,000 prize under the 1714 Longitude Act for a practical solution, which most experts believed lay in complex astronomical observations.

Harrison instead pursued a mechanical solution, spending decades developing a series of increasingly sophisticated marine chronometers that could keep precise time despite the motion, temperature changes, and humidity of a sea voyage. His final design, the H4 watch, proved astonishingly accurate during a voyage to Jamaica in 1761, revolutionising navigation and securing British maritime supremacy, though he had to fight the scientific establishment for years to claim his reward.
